"Bǎn"—
generally criticizing King Lì of Bó.
Shàngdì is unjust!
The common people are utterly weary.
Words spoken are not right,
Deeds of wickedness are not far off.
There are no wise officials, upright and distinguished;
There is no reality in what is said.
Wickedness is not far off;
Therefore, I offer great remonstrance!
Heaven is now sending down calamity;
Do not be so heedless!
Heaven is now stumbling and falling;
Do not be so remiss and negligent!
If your words were harmonious,
The people would be contented.
If your words were pleasing,
The people would submit.
Though I engage in different matters,
I am still your colleague.
I will then advise you;
Listen to my clamorous words.
My words are for your benefit;
Do not laugh at them.
The ancients had a saying:
Consult with the grass cutters and fuel gatherers!
Heaven is now sending down oppression;
Do not be so fond of jesting!
I, an old man, am earnestly advising you.
The young men are frivolous and arrogant (qiāo qiāo).
It is not that I am speaking senilely,
But you are using jesting and mockery.
Many will be scorched and burned (hè hè),
Beyond remedy!
When Heaven is stirred up with anger,
Do not engage in boasting and flattery (kuā pí).
Decorum and manners will be completely lost,
Good men will be burdened with corpses.
When the people are in a state of disorder and collapse,
Then will no one dare to turn to me?
In the chaos and turmoil, there is nothing to rely on,
Is there no one to show kindness to our army?
Heaven illuminates the people:
Like the xūn flute and the chí flute;
Like the zhāng scepter and the guī tablet;
Like taking and carrying.
Carrying, do not say it is of no benefit,
Illuminating the people is very easy,
When the people are prone to wickedness,

The good man is the fence,
The great officer is the wall,
The great state is the screen,
The great clan is the support.
Cherishing virtue brings peace,
The clan leader is the city wall.
Do not let the city wall be destroyed,
do not be alone and thus feared!
Revere Heaven's anger,
dare not be frivolous and playful.
Revere Heaven's changes,
dare not gallop wildly.
When vast Heaven says it is bright,
it is time for you to go out, O king!
When vast Heaven says it is dawn,
it is time for you to go and roam!

255 "Dàng"
"Dàng,"
Duke Mù of Zhào grieved for the great ruin of the Zhōu dynasty.
King Lì was without principle,
the world was dissolute and without principles or order,
therefore this poem was made.
Vast and boundless is God!
The protector of the people below.
Swiftly awe-inspiring is God!
His commands are often flawed?
Heaven gives birth to the multitudes of people,
are His decrees not trustworthy?
There is nothing that does not have a beginning,
but few are able to have an end!
King Wén Wáng said, "Alas!
Alas, you Yin-Shāng!
Have you ever been strong and resistant?
Have you ever been grasping and avaricious?
Have you ever been in positions of authority?
Have you ever been in positions of service?
Heaven sends down overflowing virtue,
and you rise up with this strength!
King Wén Wáng said, "Alas!
Alas, you Yin-Shāng!
You hold to righteous categories,
but are strong and resistant, full of resentment.
You use slanderous words to respond,
and thievery and plunder occur within.
The lords make covenants and curses,
without limit or end!
King Wén Wáng said, "Alas!
Alas, you Yin-Shāng!
You are arrogant and fierce in the central states,
accumulating resentment and considering it virtue.
You do not understand your virtue,
at times you have no backing and no support!
Your virtue is not understood,
You have neither attendants nor ministers!
King Wén said, "Alas!"
"Alas for you, Yin-Shāng!
Heaven does not indulge you with wine;
If you are not righteous, you will follow the pattern (of downfall)."
You have already transgressed your proper bounds,
Neither clear nor obscure,
Crying out and lamenting,
Making day as night!
King Wén said, "Alas!"
"Alas for you, Yin-Shāng!
Like cicadas and locusts,
Like boiling broth.
Small and great are nearing destruction;
People still esteem their own ways."
Great violence is done in the Central States,
Extending even to the Guǐ Fāng!
King Wén said, "Alas!"
"Alas for you, Yin-Shāng!
It is not that God does not provide the right time,
But Yin does not employ the old ways.
Although there are no experienced elders,
There are still established models.
Is it that you do not listen?
The great mandate is about to fall!"
King Wén said, "Alas!"
"Alas for you, Yin-Shāng!
People also say:"
When there is an earthquake,
Diānpèi zhī jiē, When the tree is uprooted,
zhīyè wèi yǒu hài, Before the branches and leaves are harmed,
the branches and leaves are not yet harmed,
but the root is first uprooted.
běn shí xiān bō. The root is first overthrown.
The example of Yīn is not far,
Yīn jiàn bù yuǎn, The mirror of Yīn is not far,
zài Xià hòu zhī shì! It is in the age of the Xia kings!

"Yì,"
Wèi Wǔ Gōng cì Lì Wáng, The Duke Wǔ of Wèi criticized King Lì,
yì yǐ zì jǐng yě. also used to warn himself.
Yì yì wēiyí! How dignified and solemn is his bearing!
Wéi dé zhī yú. It is the corner of virtue.
Rén yì yǒu yán: People also have a saying:
"Mí zhé bù yú. "There is no wise man who is not foolish.
Shùrén zhī yú, The foolishness of the common people,

Zhérén zhī yú, The foolishness of the wise men,

There was a man who strove for excellence,
and the four quarters followed his instructions.
He had enlightened virtue and conduct,
and the four states submitted to him.
He planned grandly and fixed decrees,
so that distant regions readily sought his counsel.
Reverent and careful in his deportment,
he was a model for the people!
But now,
there is rising confusion and disorder in government!
Overthrowing his virtue,
indulging in excessive drinking.
Though you indulge in pleasure and follow along,
do you not think of your succession?
Do not widely seek the former kings,
able to uphold their clear laws!
Thus, great Heaven does not approve!
Like that flowing spring,
do not perish together in ruin.
Rising early and sleeping late,
sweep and clean the courtyard within.
This is a pattern for the people:
repair your chariots and horses,
bows, arrows, and weapons of war.
Use them to prepare for war,
and to expel the barbarian regions.
Question your people,
be careful of your boundaries,
yòng jiè bù yú.
Shèn ěr chū huà,
jìng ěr wēiyí,
wú bù róu jiā.
Bái guī zhī diàn,
Can still be ground away.
sī yán zhī diàn,
bù kě wéi yě!
Wú yì yóu yán,
wú yuē gǒu yǐ!
Mò mēn zhèn shé,

Zǐsūn shéng shéng,

Shì ěr yǒujūnzǐ,
jí róu ěr yán,

Xiāng zài ěr shì,
shàng bù kuì yú wū lòu?
Wú yuē bù xiǎn,
mò yǔ yún gòu!"
Shén zhī gé sī,
bù kě dù sī,
shěn kě shè sī!
Pì ěr wèi dé,
bì zāng bì jiā.
Shú shèn ěr zhǐ,
that you may not err in your deportment.
Be neither presumptuous nor villainous,
and few will not take you as a model.
He throws me a peach,
I repay him with a plum.
That ox has horns while still young,
truly a rainbow [is he], that young fellow!
The flexible young tree,
is bound with thread.
The gentle and respectful person,
is the foundation of virtue.
If they are wise,
tell them instructive words,
to guide them in the practice of virtue.
If they are foolish,
they will turn around and accuse me of presumption;
people all have their own minds!
Alas, young one!
You do not yet know good from bad.
It is not by holding their hand,
that I tell them of matters.
It is not by speaking to their face,
that I lift them by their ear.
Suppose you say you do not know,
you have already held a child!
The people are not satisfied:
who knows early and does not achieve?
Vast Heaven is very bright!
My life has no joy.
I see you confused,

Instructing you earnestly,

It is not used as instruction,

Pretending to say, "I do not know,"

Alas, young one!
Tell you of the old ways.
Listen to and use my plans,
Perhaps there will be no great regret.
Heaven is now difficult,
Saying it will lose its state.
Taking an analogy is not far,
August Heaven does not err.
Turning aside from his virtue,
Causing the people great hardship?

257 "Sāng Róu"
"Sāng Róu" is a poem by Ruì Bó criticizing King Lì.
The mulberry trees are luxuriant,
Beneath them, it will soon be ten days;
The people are gathering and picking the fallen leaves.
The suffering of these lower people
Never extinguishes my heart's sorrow.
The granaries are completely full!
But the great and bright Heaven,
Does it not take pity on me?
The four steeds move quickly,
The banners and streamers flutter.
Disorder grows without ceasing,
No state is not destroyed.
The people have no black-haired descendants left;
All disasters turn them to ashes.
Alas, how sad!
The state's progress is so troubled.
The state's progress has no resources;
Heaven will not help us.
There is nowhere to stop and rest;
Where shall we go?
Indeed, the princely man
Should maintain a heart without contention.
Who created this perilous situation,
That continues to be a hindrance to this day?
My worried heart is full of grief,
I think of my land.
I was born at an inauspicious time,
féng tiān dàn nù. (encountering Heaven's great anger.)
Zì xī cú dōng, (From west to east,)
mí suǒ dìng chù. (there is no place to settle.)
Duō wǒ gòu mǐn, (Many are the calamities I encounter,)
kǒng jí wǒ yǔ. (greatly distressing my borders.)
Wèi móu wèi bì, (Though I plan and take precautions,)
luàn kuàng sī xuē. (the state of disorder is thus diminished.)
Gào ěr yōu xù, (I tell you to be concerned and distressed,)
huì ěr xù jué. (I teach you to properly order the ranks of nobility.)
Shéi néng zhí rè, (Who can hold hot things,)
shì bù yǐ zhuó? (and not use water to cool them?)
Qí hé néng shū, (How can they be good,)
zài xū jí nì? (but together go down to drowning?)
Rú bǐ sù fēng, (Like that wind blowing against one,)
yì kǒng zhī ài. (is also very difficult.)
Mín yǒu sù xīn, (The people have respectful hearts,)
píng yún bù dǎi. (but luxuriant growth is said to be unattainable.)
Hǎo shì jià sè, (Loving this planting and harvesting,)
lì mín dài shí; (encourage the people to provide food.)
Jià sè wéi bǎo, (Planting and harvesting are treasures,)
dài shí wéi hǎo. (providing food is good.)
Tiān jiàng sàng luàn, (Heaven sends down mourning and chaos,)
miè wǒ lì wáng? (to destroy our appointed king?)
Jiàng cǐ máo zéi, (It sends down these destructive insects,)
jià sè zú yǎng. (so that the crops are ultimately itchy.)
Āi tōng Zhōngguó! (Alas for suffering China!)
Are all the useless ones wholly desolate?
There is no strength to be exerted,
to be mindful of vast Heaven!
It is this kind prince!
Whom the people look up to.
Holding a mind that proclaims plans,
examining with care his ministers.
It is those who are disobedient!
Who deem themselves alone to be good.
They have their own hearts and minds,
causing the people to be wholly mad.
Look at that middle forest,
the deer thrive abundantly.
Friends have already slandered,
they do not mutually seek good.
People also have a saying:
"Advancing and retreating are both valleys!"
It is this sage!
Who looks ahead a hundred *lǐ*.
It is that fool!
Overturning madness with joy.
It's not that I can't speak,
Why am I so fearful and hesitant?
This worthy man,
He is neither sought after nor advanced.
That cruel-hearted one,
He is regarded and repeatedly employed.
The people are greedy and disorderly,
Is it better to treat them like bitter weeds?
A great wind has its tunnels,
And great valleys have hollows.
This worthy man,
His actions are models of goodness.
That disobedient one,
He is promoted because of hidden corruption.
A great wind has its tunnels,
Greedy people are a blight.
When you listen to their words, they respond cleverly,
When you recite to them, they act as if drunk.
They do not employ the good,
But instead make me act perversely!
Alas, you friends!
Is it that I do not know and act?
Like those flying insects,
They are sometimes caught with arrows.
Since you go to that scheming woman,
You turn against me with anger?
The people have no limits,
Zhí Liáng is good at betrayal!
Being unfavorable to the people,
Is like clouds that cannot bring rain?
The people's disobedience and perversity,
Is because Zhí competes in using force!
The people not yet submitting,
Is because Zhí commits theft and acts as a bandit;
Liáng says this is not permissible.
Betrayal is good at cursing,
Although you say it is not you,
You have already created your song!
"Sāng Róu" has sixteen chapters,
Eight chapters with eight lines each,
Eight chapters with six lines each.
258 《Yún Hàn》
《Yún Hàn》,
Is about Réng Shū praising King Xuān.
King Xuān inherited the ferocity of King Lì,
Internally had the ambition to correct disorder,
Encountered disasters and was fearful,
Humbly cultivated his conduct,
Wishing to dispel them.
The world rejoiced that the kingly way was restored.
The common people saw his worry,
Therefore, they composed this poem.
So vast is the Milky Way,
Shining and circling in the sky.
The King says, "Alas!
What crime have the people of today committed?
Heaven sends down ruin and disorder,
Famine and scarcity repeatedly arrive.
There is no spirit that we have not honored,
There is no sacrificial animal that we have spared.
The jade tablets and precious gems are all exhausted,
Why will you not listen to us?
The drought is already very great,
Hot and fiery, rising up.
We do not neglect the sacrifices,
From the altar in the suburbs to the ancestral temple.
Above and below, we have laid offerings and buried victims,
There is no spirit that we have not revered.
Can it be that Hòujì 后稷 is not able [to help],
That Shàngdì 上帝 does not descend?
Wasting and ruining this lower earth,
Must I alone encounter this!"
The drought is already too severe,
So that it cannot be averted?
I am reverent and cautious,
As if thunder and lightning were upon me.
The remnant people of Zhōu 周,
There are none left behind.
Oh, vast Heaven, sovereign God,
Do you not leave us behind?
Why do you not fear each other,
The former ancestors in ruin?
The drought is already too severe,
Then it cannot be stopped?
Blazing and burning,
You say I have nowhere to turn.
The great mandate is near its end!
Without looking forward or back.
The assembled dukes and senior officials,
Then do not assist me;
The father and mother, the former ancestors,
How can they bear to abandon me?
The drought is already too severe,
Sweeping clean the mountains and rivers.
The drought demon brings calamity,
Like scorching, like burning.
My heart dreads the heat,
My worried heart is like smoke.
The assembled dukes and senior officials,
Then do not hear me;
Hào Tiān Shàngdì,
How can you allow me to flee?
The drought is already too severe,
Striving, I fear to leave.
How can you afflict me with drought?
I truly do not know the reason!
We prayed for the harvest very early,
We did not neglect the altars of the four quarters.
Hào Tiān Shàngdì,
Then do not regard me;
Respectfully reverent to the bright spirits,
It should be without cause for regret or anger!
The drought is already too severe,
Scattered, without friendly alliance.
Investigate the many officials!
Grievous is the responsibility of the chief minister!
Hasten, Master of the Horse,
Chefs and attendants!
There is no one who is not attended to,
None who cannot be stopped.
Looking up to vast Heaven,
What is to become of this land?
Looking up to vast Heaven,
There are twinkling stars.
High officials and gentlemen,
Clearly pray without ceasing,
The great command is near to stopping!
Do not abandon your achievements.
What do you seek to do for me?
To pervert the many officials!
Looking up to vast Heaven,
When will you grant peace?
"Yún Hàn" has eight stanzas,
Each stanza has ten lines.
259 "Sōng Gāo"
"Sōng Gāo"
is Yǐn Jífǔ's praise of King Xuān.
The world having returned to peace,
he was able to establish states,
befriend the various lords,
and commend and reward Shēn Bó.
Sōng Gāo is a great mountain,
towering extremely to the heavens.
The great mountain sends down a spirit!
Giving birth to Fǔ and Shēn.
Both Shēn and Fǔ!
Are the support of Zhōu.
The four states become prosperous,
the four directions become peaceful.
Diligent and earnest is Shēn Bó!
He continues the affairs of the king.
At Yì and at Xiè,
he is a model for the southern states.
The king ordered Zhào Bó:
To establish the dwelling of Shēn Bó.
Ascend to this southern region,
and forever maintain his merits.
The king ordered Shēn Bó:
To be a model for this southern region.
Therefore, he thanked the people,
and used them in your service.
The king commanded Zhào Bó:
Survey Shēn Bó's lands.
The king commanded the Fù Yù:
Move his personal retinue.
Shēn Bó's accomplishments
Zhào Bó planned.
They began building his city,
The ancestral temple was completed.
Once completed, it was imposing.
The king bestowed upon Shēn Bó:
Four strong stallions,
With glistening, ornamented breastplates.
The king dispatched Shēn Bó,
With a road carriage and team of horses:
"I have planned your dwelling,
None is better than the southern lands.
I bestow upon you a large jade tablet,
To serve as your treasure.
Go near to the king's uncle!
Protect the southern lands!"
Shēn Bó confidently departed,
The king feasted him off at Méi.
Shēn Bó returned south,
Offering thanks for his successful return.
The king commanded Zhào Bó:
Survey Shēn Bó's territory,
To stockpile his provisions,
To hasten his journey.
How illustrious is Shēn Bó!
The king's maternal uncle,
A model of Wén and Wǔ!
Shēn Bó's virtue,
Gentle, kind, and upright.
He pacifies all the states,
Renowned throughout the four kingdoms.
Jí Fǔ composes a song,
Its poem is exceedingly grand.
Its style is very fine,
To present to Shēn Bó!
"Sōng Gāo" has eight stanzas,
Each stanza has eight lines.
260 "Zhēng Mín"
"Zhēng Mín" is about Yǐn Jí Fǔ praising King Xuān.
He employed the virtuous and enabled the talented,
and the Zhōu Dynasty was restored.
Heaven gives birth to the multitudes,
All things have their rules.
The people hold to their constant nature,
Loving excellent virtue.
Heaven oversees the Zhōu,
Clearly shines below,
Protecting this Son of Heaven,
Giving birth to Zhòng Shān Fǔ!
He gave birth to Zhòng Shān Fǔ!
Zhòng Shān Fǔ's virtue
was gentle and excellent, a pattern to follow:
dignified in bearing, dignified in countenance,
cautious and respectful.
He took the ancient teachings as his model,
and made dignified deportment his strength.
He obeyed the Son of Heaven,
and clearly proclaimed the commands entrusted to him.
The king charged Zhòng Shān Fǔ:
to be a model for all the officials,
to continue the work of your martial ancestors,
and to protect the king's person.
He issued and received the king's commands,
serving as the king's throat and tongue.
He promulgated policies abroad,
and all quarters responded accordingly.
Solemn were the king's commands;
Zhòng Shān Fǔ carried them out.
Whether the state was in order or in disorder,
Zhòng Shān Fǔ made it clear.
Being both wise and discerning,
he preserved his person.
From morning till night he did not slacken,
in serving the one man!
People also have a saying:
"If it is soft, then he consumes it;
if it is hard, then he spits it out."
But it is Zhòng Shānfǔ,
soft things he does not consume,
hard things he does not spit out.
He does not insult the lonely and widowed,
he does not fear the strong and the powerful!
People also have a saying:
"Virtue is as light as a feather,
but few among the people can lift it."
I measured and planned it,
and it was Zhòng Shānfǔ who lifted it,
and none loved to assist him.
If there are deficiencies in the royal duties,
it is Zhòng Shānfǔ who makes them up!
Zhòng Shānfǔ set out with a farewell ceremony,
the four steeds were sturdy,
the marching men were swift,
each thinking he could not keep up.
The four steeds were strong,
the eight bells chimed musically.
The king charged Zhòng Shānfǔ:
to build that city in the East.
The four steeds were prancing,
the eight bells rang harmoniously.
Zhòng Shānfǔ is going to Qí,
may he hasten his return.
Jí Fǔ made this ode,
grave as the clear wind.
Zhòng Shānfǔ cherishes it forever,
to comfort his heart!
"Zheng Min" consists of eight stanzas,
each stanza has eight lines.
261 "Hán Yì"
"Hán Yì"
Yǐn Jífǔ praises King Xuān.
(For his) ability to bestow mandates on the feudal lords.
Luxuriant is Mount Liáng,
Yǔ surveyed it.
Its roads were broad and clear.
The Marquis of Hán received his mandate,
The King personally bestowed it upon him:
Continue the work of your martial ancestors!
Do not neglect my command!
Day and night, never relaxing,
Reverently attend to your position,
My command is not easily changed.
Strike at the unsubmissive regions,
To assist your sovereign.
The four steeds are spirited,
So tall and strong.
Hán hóu entered to have an audience,
with his large guī-jade,
entering to have an audience with the King.
The King bestowed upon Hán hóu:
A fine flag with streamers,
a bamboo mat cover on the carriage with an ornamented crossbar.
A black gǔn-robe and red slippers,
a hooked chest-band and engraved bronze fittings.
A leather quiver and bow-case with a shallow cover,
reins with gold bands.
Hán hóu set out from his ancestral temple,
lodging overnight at Tú.
Xiǎn Fǔ saw him off with a farewell feast,
with a hundred hú of clear wine.
What were the dishes?
Roasted turtles and fresh fish.
What were the vegetables?
Bamboo shoots and cattails.
What were the gifts?
Four horses and a great carriage.
The bamboo stands and wooden vessels were abundant,
the lord's clan feasted together.
Hán hóu took a wife,
the nephew of the Lord of Fén,
the daughter of Jué Fǔ.
Hán hóu went to meet her,
Yú jué zhī lǐ. At Jué's village.
Bǎi liǎng péng péng, A hundred carriages rumble,
Bā luán qiāng qiāng, Eight bells jingle!
Bù xiǎn qí guāng? Is its glory not manifest?
Zhū dì cóng zhī, The many younger sisters follow her,
Qí qí rú yún. Crowded like clouds.
Hán hóu gù zhī, The Marquis of Hán looks upon them,
Làn qí yíng mén! Splendor fills his gate!
Jué fù kǒng wǔ! Jué fù is exceedingly martial!
Mí guó bù dào. No region is unvisited.
Wèi Hán Jí xiāng yōu, For Hán Jí he seeks a good place,
Mò rú Hán lè. Nothing is better than the lands of Hán.
Kǒng lè Hán tǔ! Greatly rejoice in the lands of Hán!
Chuān zé xū xū, The rivers and marshes are vast,
Fáng xù fǔ fǔ, The bream and whitefish are numerous,
Yōu lù yǔ yǔ. The does are bleating.
Yǒu xióng yǒu pí, There are bears and brown bears,
Yǒu māo yǒu hǔ. There are wildcats and tigers.
Qìng jì lìng jū, Auspicious is this excellent dwelling,
Hán Jí yàn yù! Hán Jí enjoys ease and praise!
Pǔ bǐ Hán chéng! Vast is that city of Hán!
Yān shī suǒ wán. Built perfectly by the troops of Yān.
Yǐ xiānzǔ shòu mìng, Because his ancestors received the mandate,
Yīn shí bǎi mán. And thus controlled the hundred tribes.
Wáng xī Hán hóu: The king bestowed upon the Marquis of Hán:
Qí zhuī qí mò, Their Zhuī and their Mò peoples,
Yǎn shòu běi guó, Entirely receiving the northern regions,
Yīn yǐ qí bó. Thereby making him its overlord.
Truly the walls and moats,
Truly the acres and fields.
They present their *pí* pelts,
Red leopards and yellow bears.
The "Hán Yì" has six stanzas,
Each stanza has twelve lines.
262 "The Jiāng and Hàn"
"The Jiāng and Hàn,"
Is Yǐn Jí-fǔ praising King Xuān.
He was able to revive the decline and quell disorder,
And ordered Duke Zhào to pacify the Huái barbarians.
The Jiāng and Hàn surge and flow,
The warriors float and drift. Not for ease, not for pleasure,
The Huái barbarians come seeking!
We have already brought out our chariots,
We have already set up our banners.
Not for ease, not for leisure,
The Huái barbarians come prostrate!
The Jiāng and Hàn are overflowing,
The warriors are brave and spirited.
Managing the four quarters,
Reporting success to the King.
The four quarters being pacified,
The royal state is thereby settled.
At this time, there was no contention,
the king's heart was filled with peace.
On the banks of the Jiāng and Hàn rivers,
the king ordered Zhào Hǔ:
"Go and open up the four quarters,
thoroughly survey our territory.
Do not be troubled or hurried,
the kingdom will reach its limit,
to the boundaries and to the governed lands,
reaching as far as the South Sea."
The king ordered Zhào Hǔ:
"Come quickly, come spread (my decree)."
Wén and Wǔ received the Mandate,
Duke Zhào is a support.
Do not say, "I am but a small one!"
Model yourself on Duke Zhào.
Initiate diligent martial affairs,
thereby I will bestow blessings upon you!
I bestow upon you a guī and a zuàn,
and a yóu of black millet wine;
to report to the accomplished men.
I bestow upon you land in the mountains,
receiving the Mandate from Zhōu,
from the ancestral commands of Zhào."
Hǔ bowed and knocked his head:
"May the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years!"
Hǔ bows and kowtows,
Praising the great kindness of the king.
May it be a model for Zhào Gōng's successors,
May the Son of Heaven live for ten thousand years!
How wise is the Son of Heaven,
His glorious reputation knows no end.
He displays his civil virtues,
Extending to these four regions!
"Jiāng Hàn," six stanzas,
Each stanza eight lines.
263 "Cháng Wǔ"
"Cháng Wǔ,"
(is a poem) by Zhào Mùgōng, praising King Xuān.
(It describes how he) establishes military affairs with constant virtue,
And uses this as a warning.
Brilliant and clear,
The king commands his ministers,
Nán Zhòng, the grand ancestor;
Tàishī Huángfǔ.
Organize my six armies,
To cultivate our military affairs.
With reverence and caution,
Bring peace to this southern region!
The king said to the Yǐn clan,
Commanding Chéng Bó Xiūfù:
Line up to the left and right,
Prepare our troops!
Advance along the banks of the Huái River,
Inspect this territory of Xú.
Do not tarry, do not settle down!
The three affairs are in order!
With blazing majesty,
Stands the awe-inspiring Son of Heaven!
The King is securing his achievements:
Not for succession, not for pleasure trips,
But because the lands of Xú are in constant turmoil!
Shaking and terrifying the lands of Xú,
Like thunder and lightning,
The lands of Xú are terrified!
The King rouses his martial spirit!
Like thunder, like rage.
He advances his valiant ministers,
Fierce like roaring tigers.
They spread out along the banks of the Huái,
And capture those ugly prisoners.
Cutting across the banks of the Huái,
Where the King's army is!
The King's army advances in great numbers!
Like flying birds,
Like the Jiāng and Hàn Rivers.
Like a mountain covered in vegetation,
Like the flow of a river.
Continuously and orderly,
Unfathomable and unconquerable,
we wash and attack the state of Xú!
The king indeed approves the barrier!
The lands of Xú have come.
The lands of Xú are now united,
it is the Son of Heaven's accomplishment!
The four quarters are now pacified,
the lands of Xú come to court.
The lands of Xú do not turn back,
the king says, "Let them return home!"
"Cháng Wǔ" has six stanzas,
each stanza has eight lines.
264 "Zhān Áng"
"Zhān Áng",
Fán Bó satirizes King Yōu's great ruin.
Gazing up, vast Heaven!
Will you not favor us?
Greatly troubled and unpeaceful,
you send down this great calamity!
The state has no stability,
the officers and people are weary.
The *mao* bandits and *mao* diseases,
have no just limit.
The nets of crime are not drawn in,
there is no just recovery!
People have land,
but the woman instead possesses it.
People have servants,
but the woman completely seizes them.
These should be innocent,
but the woman instead arrests them.
Those should be guilty,
but the woman completely releases them.
A wise man builds a city,
a wise woman overthrows a city.
Admirable is that wise woman!
She becomes an owl or a kite.
A woman has a long tongue;
it is the stairs to calamity.
Disorder does not descend from heaven;
it is born from women.
Neither teaching nor guidance,
but instead eunuchs!
To interrogate people with resentment and malice,
slandering from beginning to end.
How can you say it's not excessive,
what is the reason for such wickedness?
Like a merchant's three-fold profit,
a gentleman recognizes this;
women have no public affairs;
why not let them rest from their silkworm rearing and weaving?
Why does Heaven punish?
Hé shén bù fù? What god is not generous?
Shě ěr jiè Dí, Why do you abandon these bordering Dí peoples,
Wéi yǔ xū jì? And only make me the object of your hate?
Bù diào bù xiáng, Without pity, without auspiciousness,
Wēiyí bù lèi. Deportment is not appropriate.
Rén zhī yúnwáng, The people are perishing,
Bāngguó tiǎn cuì! The state is utterly exhausted!
Tiān zhī jiàng wǎng, Heaven sends down a net,
Wéi qí yōu yǐ? How extensive it is!
Rén zhī yúnwáng, The people are perishing,
Xīn zhī yōu yǐ! My heart is full of sorrow!
Tiān zhī jiàng wǎng, Heaven sends down a net,
Wéi qí jī yǐ? How close it is!
Rén zhī yúnwáng, The people are perishing,
Xīn zhī bēi yǐ! My heart is full of grief!
Bìfèi kǎn quán, The gushing spring from the ravine,
Wéi qí shēn yǐ? How deep it is!
Xīn zhī yōu yǐ, My heart is full of sorrow,
Níng zì jīn yǐ: Would that it ended today:
Bù zì wǒ xiān, Not before me,
Bù zì wǒ hòu! Not after me!
Miǎomiǎo hàotiān, Vast and distant Heaven,
Wú bù kè gǒng. There is nothing you cannot consolidate.
Wú tiǎn huángzǔ, Do not disgrace your ancestors,
Shì jiù ěr hòu! And so save your descendants!
"Zhān Áng" has seven stanzas,
Three stanzas have ten lines each,
Four stanzas have eight lines each.
265 "Zhào Mín"
"Zhào Mín"—
Fán Bó satirizes Yōu Wáng's great ruin.
Mín means "to pity."
It is to pity that the world has no minister like Zhào Gōng.
O vast heaven, your wrath is swift!
Heaven has truly sent down calamity.
It has afflicted us with famine and dearth,
So that the people utterly flee and perish,
And where I dwell, the borders are all desolate!
Heaven sends down nets of crime!
The mou and zei are in internal strife.
Dark and stupid, they contribute nothing,
Rushing along and turning to evil,
How can they really secure and tranquillize my state?
They babble and slander,
And do not even know their faults!
I am reverent and cautious,
But there is great and constant disquiet,
And my office is greatly reduced!
It is like a year of drought,
When the grass does not luxuriantly grow,
Like a nest of dry grass.
That I should be minister of this state,
And that nothing should but come to ruin!
The former wealth,
is not like the present time!
The present troubles,
are not like these!
Those are careless and these are refined,
why not replace yourselves?
It is the elder brothers who lead us to this!
The pool is dried up,
it is not said to be from frequent use.
The spring is dried up,
it is not said to be from the middle itself.
The widespread harm!
It is the elder brothers who make it great,
will it not bring disaster to my person?
Formerly, the former kings received the Mandate,
as with the Duke of Shào (Shào Gōng).
Daily, they enlarged the country a hundred *lǐ*,
now, daily the country shrinks a hundred *lǐ*.
Alas, alas!
The people of today,
do they not value the old ways?
"Zhào Mín" has seven stanzas,
four stanzas have five lines each,
three stanzas have seven lines each.
The "Dàng zhī Shí" has eleven poems,
ninety-two stanzas,
seven hundred and sixty-nine lines.
Zhōu Sòng Qīng Miào zhī Shí Dì Yī
266 "Qīng Miào"
"Qīng Miào"
is for sacrificing to Wén Wáng.
Zhōu Gōng having completed Luòyì,
held court with the various feudal lords,
leading them in sacrificing to Wén Wáng.
Oh, solemn and pure temple!
Reverent and harmonious are the illustrious assistants,
numerous and accomplished are the officers,
upholding the virtue of Wén.
Responding to those on high,
swiftly they hasten in the temple.
Is it not manifest and carried on?
Let there be no satiety among these men!
"Qīng Miào," one stanza,
eight lines.
267 "Wéi Tiān zhī Mìng"
"Wéi Tiān zhī Mìng"
is a grand declaration to Wén Wáng in a time of great peace.
The mandate of Heaven,
how solemn and unceasing!
Oh, how illustrious
is the purity of Wén Wáng's virtue!
Bestow it abundantly upon us?
We shall receive it.
Greatly favor our Wén Wáng,
may his great-grandson strengthen it!
"Wéi Tiān zhī Mìng" (維天之命), one chapter,
eight lines.
268 "Wéi Qīng" (維清)
"Wéi Qīng" (維清),
a dance performed with ivory instruments.
Oh, pure and bright,
the laws of King Wén (Wén Wáng),
commencing the sacrifice.
To complete them and achieve success,
is the good fortune of Zhōu! (周)
"Wéi Qīng" (維清), one chapter,
five lines.
269 "Liè Wén" (烈文)
"Liè Wén" (烈文),
when King Chéng (Chéng Wáng) took office,
the lords assisted in the sacrifice.
Illustrious and splendid are you, princely lords!
Bestowing on you these blessings and happiness.
Favor us with boundless blessings,
that your descendants may preserve them.
Do not set limits to your state;
may the king exalt it!
thirteen lines.
270 "Heaven Made"
"Heaven Made,"
is for sacrificing to former kings and former dukes.
Heaven made the high mountains,
Dà Wáng cleared them.
He commenced it,
Wén Wáng brought peace to it.
He departed,
Qí had its even paths.
May descendants preserve it!
"Tiān Zuò" chapter,
seven lines.
271 "Hào Tiān Yǒu Chéng Mìng"
"Hào Tiān Yǒu Chéng Mìng"
is for suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth.
August Heaven has conferred a completed mandate;
the two lords received it.
Chéng Wáng dared not be at ease;
day and night he built upon the mandate in silence.
Oh, how bright!
Singly pursue his heart.
Thus put to rest the country!
"Hào Tiān Yǒu Chéng Mìng" chapter,
seven lines.
272 "Wǒ Jiāng"
"Wǒ Jiāng"
is for sacrificing to Wén Wáng in the Bright Hall.
I will offer, I will enjoy;
sheep and oxen are provided,
may Heaven aid us!
According to the model of Wén Wáng's ceremonies,
Rì jìng sìfāng. The sun pacifies the four quarters.
Yī gǔ Wén Wáng! Oh, great and grand King Wén!
Jì yòu xiǎng zhī. He has already assisted in the offerings to him.
Wǒ qí sù yè, Let me be diligent day and night,
Wèi tiān zhī wēi. Fearing the majesty of Heaven.
Yú shí bǎo zhī! Thereby to preserve it!
"Wǒ Jiāng" one chapter, "Wǒ Jiāng" (I Will) one chapter,
ten sentences. ten sentences.
273 "Shí Mài"
"Shí Mài", "Shí Mài" (The Season Advances),
Xúnshǒu gàojì chái wàng yě. (is a song for) the emperor's tour of inspection and reporting sacrifices, firewood sacrifices, and distant sacrifices.
Shí mài qí bāng, When he travels through his states,
Hàotiān qí zǐ zhī, Hàotiān (August Heaven) approves of his son,
Shí yòu xù yǒu Zhōu. Indeed assisting in ordering the houses of Zhōu.
Bó yán zhèn zhī, A slight word shakes them,
Mò bù zhèn dié. None do not tremble with awe.
Huáiróu bǎi shén, Cherishing and pacifying the hundred spirits,
Jí Hé Qiáo Yuè, Reaching the Yellow River and tall mountains,
Yǔn wáng wéi hòu! Truly the king is a sovereign!
Míng zhāo yǒu Zhōu, Brightly illuminating the houses of Zhōu,
Shì xù zài wèi. Thus ordering those in positions.
Zài jí gāngē, Then store the shields and spears,
Zài gāo gōngshǐ. Then sheath the bows and arrows.
Wǒ qiú yì dé, I seek excellent virtue,
Sì yú shí xià, Extending it to these Xia,
Yǔn Wáng bǎo zhī! King Yǔn protects them!
“Shí Mài”, one chapter,
fifteen lines.
274 "Zhí Jìng"
"Zhí Jìng"
Sacrifice to King Wǔ.
Zhí jìng Wǔ Wáng! King Wǔ was truly diligent!
Wú jìng wéi liè. His excellence was unsurpassed.
Bù xiǎn Chéng Kāng, The accomplishments of Chéng and Kāng were manifest,
Shàngdì shì huáng! God on high approved of them!
Zì bǐ Chéng Kāng, From the time of Chéng and Kāng,
yǎn yǒu sì fāng, They possessed all the regions,
jīn jīn qí míng. How very bright was their wisdom.
Zhōng gǔ huáng huáng, The bells and drums sound grandly,
qìng guǎn jiāng jiāng, The chimes and pipes are majestic,
jiàng fú ráng ráng! Decreasing blessings abundantly!
Jiàng fú jiǎn jiǎn, Decreasing blessings generously,
wēi yí fǎn fǎn. Their dignified bearing is proper.
Jì zuì jì bǎo, Having been satiated with drink and food,
fú lù lái fǎn! Blessings and emoluments come back!
"Zhí Jìng", one chapter,
fourteen lines.
275 "Sī Wén"
"Sī Wén"
describes Hòu Jì being matched with Heaven.
Oh, thoughtful and cultured is Hòu Jì!
He is able to be matched with that Heaven.
He establishes our multitudes,
none are not due to your standard.
You bequeathed to us the wheat and barley,
the Emperor commanded their universal nurture,
without this boundary or your limit,
setting forth the constant principles in this Xià.
"Sī Wén," one chapter,
eight lines.
The "Qīng Miào zhī Shí" consists of ten pieces,
ten chapters,
ninety-five lines.
The second of the Zhou Hymns, "Chén Gōng zhī Shí"
276 "Chén Gōng"
"Chén Gōng"
describes the feudal lords assisting in the sacrifice,
being sent to the temple.
Alas, you officials!
Reverently attend to your duties in public.
The King bestows rewards according to your accomplishments,
coming to consult and deliberate:
Alas, you guardians!
In the last month of spring.
What more could one seek?
How about the newly tilled fields?
Oh, the great wheat and barley!
Will receive its brightness.
Brightness shines on God.
Until we have a year of plenty.
Command our people:
Prepare your hoes and plows,
Hasten to observe the sickles and weeding hoes!
"Chén Gōng" (Ministers) one chapter,
fifteen lines.
277 "Yī Xī" (Alas)
"Yī Xī" (Alas),
It is praying for grain to God in spring and summer.
Yī Xī (Alas), King Chéng!
Already you have brightly received (the mandate).
Lead the farmers of the season,
Sow your hundred grains.
Quickly develop your private fields,
Reaching thirty *lǐ*;
Also attend to your plowing,
Ten thousand are in pairs!
"Yī Xī" (Alas) one chapter,
eight lines.
278 "Zhèn Lù" (Fluttering Herons)
"Zhèn Lù" (Fluttering Herons),
refers to the descendants of the Èr Wáng who come to assist in the sacrifices.
The egrets fly with flapping wings,
towards that Western Yōng.
Our guests arrive and stop,
and there is also such ceremony.
There, we do no wrong,
Here, we are not wearied.
Hoping for early and late diligence,
to forever end with praise.
chapter,
eight lines.
279 "Fēng Nián"
"Fēng Nián"
refers to the autumn and winter reporting (of harvest).
Abundant years bring much millet and rice!
There are also tall granaries,
containing myriad millions and zǐ.
Preparing wine and sweet wine,
respectfully presenting them to our ancestors.
In order to accord with all the rites,
may blessings descend abundantly!
"Fēngnián" (Abundant Year) one chapter,
seven lines.
280 "Yǒu Gǔ" (There are Blind Musicians)
"Yǒu Gǔ,"
(describes) the beginning of music-making and harmonizing with the ancestors.
There are blind musicians, there are blind musicians!
In the court of Zhōu.
Setting up the great stands and the bell frames,
the layered frames and feathered ornaments.
Responding to the filled and hung drums,
the small drums, sounding stones, the starter and stopper instruments.
Once all is prepared, then the music is played,
the panpipes and flutes are all raised.
Loud and resonant are their sounds,
solemn, harmonious, and concordant,
the ancestors are listening!
Our guests arrive and stop,
to forever witness its completion!
"Yǒu Gǔ" one chapter,
thirteen lines.
281 *Qián*
*Qián*:
In the last month of winter, fish are offered;
in spring, sturgeon is presented.
Oh, the *Qī* and *Jǔ* rivers!
The *Qián* River has many fish:
there are sturgeon and great sturgeon,
*tiáo*, *cháng*, *yǎn*, and carp.
With these, we feast and sacrifice,
to seek great blessings!
*Qián*: one stanza,
six lines.
282 *Yōng*
*Yōng*:
(A song for) the *dì* sacrifice to the great ancestor.
They come harmoniously,
arriving respectfully.
Assisting are the dukes,
the Son of Heaven solemn.
They offer the great bull!
Together they perform the great sacrifice.
Excellent, indeed, are our august deceased fathers!
They comfort us, their filial sons.
His wisdom and discernment made him a man,
his civil and martial virtues made her a queen.
They feast and reach to august Heaven,
and are able to make their descendants prosper.
They grant us long life,
and bestow upon us abundant blessings!
They assist our accomplished deceased father,
and also assist our accomplished civil mother!
The "Yōng" ode, one chapter,
sixteen lines.
283 "Zài Jiàn"
"Zài Jiàn,"
(describes) when the various feudal lords first appeared at the temple of King Wǔ.
They meet with the ancestral king,
and say they seek his mandate:
The dragon flags fly bright,
the harmonious bells ring loudly.
The reins and straps have decorations,
how glorious and bright they are!
They lead to see the enlightened deceased father,
with filial piety and offerings.
In order to increase (our) longevity,
forever preserving it.
We think of the great blessings!
The accomplished civil ancestral duke,
bestows much fortune upon us,
causing (us) to constantly shine in pure happiness!
The "Zài Jiàn" ode, one chapter,
fourteen lines.
284 "Yǒu Kè"
"Yǒu Kè,"
(tells of) Wēi Zǐ coming to see the ancestral temple.
There are visitors, there are visitors!
And their horses are white.
How abundant! How stately!
How solid and grand are their companies!
There are visitors lodging,
there are visitors truly sincere.
They give them halters,
to halter their horses.
We hasten to pursue them,
and on the left and right soothe them.
Having such excessive majesty,
they send down blessings that are very great!
"Yǒu Kè," one chapter,
twelve lines.
"Wǔ,"
(is a piece performed when) playing the "Dà Wǔ."
Oh! August was King Wǔ!
Incomparable was his merit.
Truly accomplished was King Wén!
He was able to open up (the way) for his successors.
Continuing the martial (legacy), receiving it,
Conquering Yīn and stopping the flow,
Greatly settling your achievements.
"Wǔ", one chapter,
seven lines.
"Chén Gōng zhī Shí", ten pieces,
ten chapters, one hundred and six lines.
Zhōu Hymns, The Tenth of "Mǐn Yǔ Xiǎozi", the third.
286 "Mǐn Yǔ Xiǎozi".
"Mǐn Yǔ Xiǎozi,"
(a hymn for) when the successor-king pays court in the ancestral temple.
Alas, for me, the little child!
I have encountered a time of disorder in my family,
With anxious thoughts of guilt.
Oh, my august deceased father!
Through endless ages, I will be able to be filial.
I think of my august ancestor!
Ascending and descending in the court, I pause.
I am but a small child!
Morning and night, I am reverent.
Oh, great king!
Continuing the succession, I will not forget your example.
"Mǐn Yǔ Xiǎo Zi" (Pity Me, the Little One), one section,
eleven lines.
287 "Fǎng Luò" (Seeking Counsel)
"Fǎng Luò,"
The succeeding king consults in the ancestral temple.
Seeking my place to rest:
Following the example of my enlightened deceased father.
Oh, how long and far-reaching!
I have not yet achieved competence.
Intending to approach his accomplishments,
The succession still seems scattered and disordered.
I am but a small child!
Unable to bear the many difficulties of the state.
Inheriting the court, both high and low,
Ascending and descending in my home:
How excellent was my deceased father!
In preserving and clarifying his person.
"Fǎng Luò" (Seeking Counsel), one section,
twelve lines.
288 "Jìng Zhī" (Revere It)
"Jìng Zhī,"
The ministers present warnings to the succeeding king.
Be reverent, be reverent!
Heaven is greatly discerning;
its mandate is not easily maintained!
Do not say,
"He is high, high above,"
ascending and descending among his officers;
the sun watches him here.
I am but a little child!
How can I be intelligent and respectful?
Day by day, month by month,
may my learning be enriched with brightness.
Help me now to bear the burden,
and show me your illustrious virtuous conduct!
*Jìng Zhī*, one chapter,
twelve lines.
289 *Xiǎo Bì*
*Xiǎo Bì*:
It is when the succeeding king seeks assistance.
I will punish,
And prevent future troubles.
Do not invite the sting of bees;
You will only seek bitter pain.
You began by allowing those peach-eating insects,
to become rapidly flying birds.
If I cannot bear that my family has many troubles,
why do I gather in the smartweed?
"Xiǎo Bì" (Small Caution) is one chapter,
containing eight lines.
290 "Zǎi Shān" (Clearing Away)
"Zǎi Shān" is about
the spring plowing of the royal fields and praying to the gods of the land and grain.
Clearing away and cutting down,
how diligently they plow the fields!
A thousand pairs work at the weeding,
going to the low and the raised fields.
Lords preside and earls,
assistants and officers,
the strong and those that are used to it.
Loudly they cheer those bringing food,
thinking to please their wives,
and to rely on their men.
Some lay aside their plows,
and begin to work on the southern acres.
They sow all the grains,
truly containing the seeds of life.
Luxuriantly they grow,
abundantly rising in the seedlings.
Thickly grow the shoots,
continuously spreading afar.
The harvest is abundant,
truly full is their storage,
in the tens of thousands of millions and even zǐ (a large number).
It is made into wine and sweet wine,
steaming it is offered to our ancestors,
to accord with the hundred rites.
There is a rich fragrance,
the glory of the state and the family!
There is the fragrance of pepper,
bringing peace to the long-lived deceased!
Not only this, but also that,
not only today, but also today,
from ancient times until now, it has been like this!
"Zài Shān," one chapter,
thirty-one lines.
291 "Liáng Sì"
"Liáng Sì,"
is a autumn report to the gods of earth and grain.
Sharply gleam the good plows!
They begin to work the southern fields.
Sowing their various grains,
Truly filling this living thing.
Some come to see you:
Carrying baskets and round baskets,
Their provisions are foxtail millet.
Their rain hats are neatly woven,
Their hoes are sharp,
To weed out the bitter herbs and smartweed.
When the bitter herbs and smartweed are decayed,
The millet and sorghum will grow luxuriantly.
Harvesting them with quick movements,
Stacking them up high and dense.
Their height is like a city wall,
Their arrangement is like a comb,
To open up a hundred rooms.
The hundred rooms are filled,
Wives and children are at peace.
Slaughtering a dark-red bull at the appointed time,
Some have curved horns.
To resemble and to continue,
To continue the people of ancient times!
"Liáng Sì" (Good Plows), one chapter,
twenty-three lines.
292 "Sī Yī" (Silken Robes)
"Sī Yī" (Silken Robes),
is for dismissing the guest representing the dead.
Gāo Zǐ said:
It is for the spirit of the star Líng Xīng.
The silk robes are so fine!
The cap is properly worn.
From the hall to the base of the altar,
From the sheep to the bull,
The large cauldron and the small tripod.
The rhinoceros horn goblet is so curved,
The fine wine is desired to be mild.
Not clamorous, not arrogant,
How blessed is the long life!"
"Sī Yī" (Silk Garments), one chapter,
nine lines.
293 "Zhuó" (Ladle)
"Zhuó" (Ladle)
is the completion of the Dà Wǔ (Great Martial) dance.
It speaks of being able to ladle out the ways of the ancestors to nourish the world.
"Oh, illustrious are the king's troops!
Following the path of nourishing in times of obscurity.
The time is now purely bright,
Therefore, we use great assistance.
We, the dragons, receive it,
Great is the king's creation;
Carrying on with successors,
Indeed, it is you, lords,
Truly exemplary!"
"Zhuó" (Ladle), one chapter,
nine lines.
294 "Huán"
"Huán,"
is a type of mà sacrifice after military exercises.
Huán refers to martial ambition.
Pacifying the myriad states,
accumulating abundant harvests,
Heaven's mandate is not relinquished.
Majestic is King Wǔ!
He possesses his officers,
thereby secures the four quarters;
and establishes his homes.
Oh, illustrious in Heaven,
the great sovereign inspects them!
The "Huán" ode,
has nine lines.
"Lài,"
is a great conferral of honors in the temple.
Lài means to bestow.
It speaks of how rewards are given to good people.
King Wén has already diligently ceased!
We should receive it.
Spreading this, we further contemplate:
We hasten to seek stability,
時周之命。 It is the mandate of the Zhōu 周 Dynasty.
於繹思！ Oh, constantly contemplate!
《Lài》《賚》 yī zhāng, The *Lài* (Reward) chapter,
六句。 Six lines.
296 《Bān》《般》 296 *Bān* (Great).
《Bān》《般》、 *Bān* (Great) refers to:
巡守而祀四嶽河海也。 Inspecting the territories and sacrificing to the Four Peaks, rivers, and seas.
於皇時周！ Oh, glorious Zhōu 周 Dynasty!
陟其高山， Ascending its high mountains,
嶞山喬嶽； Lofty mountains and high peaks;
允猶翕河。 Truly uniting the rivers.
敷天之下， Throughout all under Heaven,
裒時之對， Gathering responses from all times,
時周之命！ It is the mandate of the Zhōu 周 Dynasty!
《Bān》《般》 yī zhāng, The *Bān* (Great) chapter,
七句。 Seven lines.
《Mǐn Yǔ Xiǎo Zǐ zhī Shí》《閔予小子之什》十一篇， The "Decade of Compassion for Me, the Little Child" consists of eleven poems,
十一章， Eleven chapters,
百三十七句。 One hundred and thirty-seven lines.
Lǔ Sòng Qióng zhī Shí 魯頌駉之什 The "Decade of Abundant Horses" from the Odes of Lǔ 魯
297 《Qióng》《駉》 297 *Qióng* (Abundant Horses).
《Qióng》《駉》、 *Qióng* (Abundant Horses):
an ode to Duke Xī (僖公).
Duke Xī was able to follow the laws of Bó Qín (伯禽),
being frugal enough for sufficiency,
and generous in loving the people,
diligent in agriculture and valuing grains,
pasturing in the open fields;
the people of Lǔ (魯) revered him.
Therefore, Jì Sūn Xíng Fǔ (季孫行父) requested an order from the Zhou court, and Shǐ Kè (史克) composed this ode.
Fat and strong are the grazing horses,
in the open fields.
Who are these grazers?
There are black horses with white markings and yellow horses,
there are black horses and yellow horses,
their chariots rumble loudly.
Our thoughts are boundless:
We think of these horses as excellent!
Fat and strong are the grazing horses!
In the open fields.
Who are these grazers?
There are dapple-gray horses and piebald horses,
There are red horses, there are black-green horses,
With the chariots moving steadily.
Our thoughts have no limit:
We think of the horses and their talent!
How numerous the herds of horses!
In the fields of the open country.
Who are those herding them?
There are white-spotted horses, there are white-maned black horses,
There are dark red horses, there are black-maned white horses,
With the chariots moving continuously.
Our thoughts have no end:
We think of the horses and their work!
How numerous the herds of horses!
In the fields of the open country.
Who are those herding them?
There are dark gray horses, there are reddish-white horses,
There are snorting horses, there are fish-like horses,
With the chariots moving swiftly.
Our thoughts are without error:
We think of the horses and their going forth!
"Jiōng" has four stanzas,
Each stanza has eight lines.
298 "Yǒu Bì"
"Yǒu Bì,"
Is a hymn praising the virtuous governance of Gōng Xī (Gōng Xī) and his ministers.
How full and abundant!
Abundant are those riding yellow horses.
They serve the public day and night,
Serving the public with clarity.
How fluttering the egrets!
Egrets are below.
The drums sound *yē yē*,
Drunk, they speak of dancing.
How joyful it is together!
How full and abundant!
Abundant are those riding stallions.
From morning till night at public affairs,
At public affairs, drinking wine.
How the egrets stir!
Egrets take flight.
The drums sound *yē yē*,
Drunk, they speak of returning.
How joyful it is together!
How full and abundant!
Abundant are those riding dark bay horses.
From morning till night at public affairs,
At public affairs, feasting.
From now on,
May the year be fruitful!
The lord has grain,
To bequeath to his grandsons.
How joyful it is together!
"Yǒu Bì" has three stanzas,
Each stanza has nine lines.
299 "Pàn Shuǐ"
"Pàn Shuǐ" (The Half-Pool),
is a hymn praising Duke Xī (Xī Gōng)'s ability to renovate the Half-Pool Palace (Pàn Gōng).
Longing to rejoice in the Pàn River!
We lightly gather its celery.
The Lord of Lǔ (魯, Lǔ) arrives and halts,
Observing his banners.
His banners are luxuriant,
The bells on the carriage jingling.
No matter small or large,
We follow the Duke in his progress.
Longing to rejoice in the Pàn River!
We lightly gather its algae.
The Lord of Lǔ arrives and halts,
His horses are strong and spirited.
His horses are strong and spirited?
Their sounds are clear and bright:
Full of dignified expression and laughter,
Not in anger, but teaching.
Longing to rejoice in the Pàn River!
We lightly gather its water caltrop.
The Lord of Lǔ arrives and halts,
Drinking wine in the Pàn.
Having drunk the delicious wine,
May he be forever granted lasting life!
Following the great path,
Subduing these many villains!
Reverent and dignified is the Lord of Lǔ!
Respectfully illuminating his virtue.
Respectfully cautious in his deportment,
He is a model for the people.
Truly accomplished in both civil and military affairs!
He clearly appeals to his glorious ancestors.
There is no one who is not filial;
He himself seeks great blessings.
Bright and clear is the Lord of Lǔ (Lǔ Hóu)!
He is able to illuminate his virtue.
Having built the Bàngōng,
The Huái barbarians submitted.
Strong and mighty are his tiger-like ministers!
At the Bàn, they offer up the captured heads.
His good counsel is like that of Gāo Yáo,
At the Pàn, they present the captives.
Numerous and accomplished are his many officers!
Able to broaden their virtuous hearts.
Mighty and martial in his expeditions,
He chastises those southeastern barbarians.
Great and resplendent!
Neither boastful nor arrogant.
Without proclaiming his quarrels,
At the Pàn, he presents his achievements.
The horn bows are strong,
The bound arrows are well-feathered.
The war chariots were very numerous,
The foot soldiers and drivers were tireless.
Having conquered the Huái Barbarians,
They were very good and offered no resistance.
Thus we strengthened your plans,
And the Huái Barbarians were completely captured.
Swiftly fly those owls,
Gathering in the Pàn forest.
They eat my mulberry fruits,
Cherishing my good sounds.
The enlightened Huái Barbarians,
Came to present their treasures:
Dark tortoise shells and ivory,
Great gifts of southern metal.
"Pàn Shuǐ" has eight stanzas,
Each stanza has eight lines.
300 "Bì Gōng"
"Bì Gōng,"
This praises Gōng Xīgōng for being able to restore the dwelling of Zhōu Gōng.
The silent temple stands profound!
Truly solid and countless.
Majestic Jiāng Yuán!
Her virtue did not deviate,
She relied on God.
Without calamity or harm,
Giving birth after a full month without delay.
Thus was born Hòu Jì,
Bestowing upon him all blessings:
Millet, glutinous millet, heavy crops,
Early and late-maturing beans and wheat.
He possessed all the lower states,
Causing the people to sow and reap.
There was millet, there was glutinous millet,
There was rice, there was black millet.
He possessed all the lower land,
Continuing the legacy of Yǔ.
The grandson of Hòu Jì,
Was truly the Great King (Dà Wáng).
Dwelling on the sunny side of Qí,
He first began to diminish the Shāng.
As for Wén Wǔ,
They continued the legacy of the Great King (Dà Wáng).
Reaching the limit of Heaven,
At the fields of Mù:
Wú èr wú yú! (Be) without duplicity, without anxiety!
Shàngdì lín nǚ. God is watching you.
Dūn Shāng zhī lǚ, You strengthened the journey of Shang,
Kè xián jué gōng. and were able to complete all their achievements.
Wáng yuē Shūfù! The King said, "Uncle!"
Jiàn ěr yuánzǐ, Establish your eldest son,
Bǐ hóu yú Lǔ. to be a marquis in Lu.
Dà qǐ ěr yǔ, Greatly expand your territory,
Wèi Zhōu shì fǔ. to be a support to the House of Zhou.
Nǎi mìng Lǔ Gōng, Thereupon he commanded the Duke of Lu,
Bǐ hóu yú dōng. to be a marquis in the east.
Xī zhī shānchuān, He bestowed upon him mountains and rivers,
Tǔtián fùyōng. land, fields, and dependent states.
Zhōu Gōng zhī sūn, Grandson of the Duke of Zhou,
Zhuāng Gōng zhī zǐ. Son of Duke Zhuang.
Lóng qí chéng sì, Dragon banners receive the sacrifices,
Liù pèi ěr ěr. The six reins are flowing and orderly.
Chūnqiū fěi jiě, In spring and autumn without fail,
Xiǎng sì bù tè: The sacrifices are enjoyed without error:
Huáng huáng hòu Dì! August and majestic is God!
Huáng zǔ Hòu Jì! August ancestor, Hòu Jì!
Xiǎng yǐ xīng xī, We offer a red bull as sacrifice,
Shì xiǎng shì yí, It is enjoyed and deemed appropriate,
Jiàng fú jì duō. The blessings bestowed are abundant.
Zhōu Gōng huáng zǔ, The Duke of Zhou, august ancestor,
Yì qí fú nǚ. also blesses you.
In autumn, they load the offerings;
In summer, they prepare the stalls and crossbars.
White bulls and red-haired bulls,
The sacrificial vessels are large and full.
Roasted meats and thick soups,
The bamboo dishes and wooden stands are greatly arrayed.
The myriad dances are vast and flowing,
The filial grandson receives blessings.
May you be blazing and prosperous,
May you be long-lived and virtuous.
Protect that eastern region!
The state of Lǔ is constant.
Not diminished, not collapsed,
Not shaken, not soaring.
May the three longevity stars be your companions,
Like hills and like mountains.
The duke's chariots number a thousand,
With red tassels and green bindings,
Two spears and heavy bows.
The duke's soldiers number thirty thousand,
With shell helmets and red cords,
The multitude is ever-increasing.
The Róng and Dí are subdued,
The Jīng and Shū are punished,
Then none dare resist us!
May you be prosperous and blazing,
May you be long-lived and wealthy.
Yellow hair and a back like a platform,
may your longevity be like Xū and Shì.
May you flourish and grow great,
may you live to be old and aged.
Ten thousand and a thousand years,
may your long life be without harm!
Mount Tài is towering,
watched over by the state of Lǔ:
possessing entirely Guī Méng,
thus opening up the great east.
Reaching to the coastal states,
the Huái barbarians come to join.
None do not follow and obey,
this is the achievement of the Marquis of Lǔ!
Holding securely Fú and Yì,
thus opening up the dwellings of Xú,
reaching to the coastal states,
the Huái barbarians and the Mán and Mò tribes.
And reaching those Southern barbarians,
none do not follow and obey,
none dare to refuse,
the Marquis of Lǔ they follow!
Heaven grants the duke pure blessings!
Long life protects Lǔ.
Abiding in constancy with indulgence,
restoring the house of the Duke of Zhōu.
The Marquis of Lǔ feasts joyfully,
may his excellent wife be a long-lived mother.
Suitable are the high officials and numerous officers,
The states and regions are thus established.
They have greatly received blessings,
With yellow hair and children's teeth!
The pines of Cúlái,
The cypresses of Xīnfǔ,
These are felled, these are measured,
These are fathomed, these are footed.
The pine rafters are massive!
The main hall is exceedingly grand,
The new temple is splendid.
What Xī Sī has made:
How vast and great,
The myriad people admire!
"Bì Gōng" has eight chapters,
Two chapters have seventeen lines each,
One chapter has twelve lines,
One chapter has thirty-eight lines,
Two chapters have eight lines each,
Two chapters have ten lines each.
"Jiōng" has four sections,
Twenty-three chapters,
Two hundred and forty-three lines.
Shāng Hymns
《Nà》,
(is a hymn) to sacrifice to Chéng Tāng.
From Wēi Zǐ to Dài Gōng,
in between, ritual and music were abandoned and decayed.
There was Zhèng Kǎo Fǔ who obtained twelve chapters of the 《Shāng Sòng》 from the Grand Music Master of Zhōu,
with 《Nà》 as the first.
Oh, how harmonious and grand!
Set up my small drums and large drums.
Play the drums with resounding beats,
to please my glorious ancestors.
May the descendant of Tāng present (the offering),
and grant us peace to complete our thoughts!
The small drums and large drums sound deep and resonant,
the pipes give forth clear and bright sounds.
Being harmonious and even,
in accordance with the sound of my chime stones.
Oh, glorious descendant of Tāng!
How reverent is your sound:
the drums are tirelessly beaten,
the myriad dances are stately and grand.
I have honored guests,
are you not also pleased and joyful?
From ancient times in the past,
the former people had accomplishments.
Being gentle and respectful morning and evening,
performing their duties with reverence.
Considering that I steam and offer sacrifices in autumn and winter,
A descendant of Tāng is about to assist!
The "Nà" chapter,
Twenty-two lines.
302 "Liè Zǔ" (Illustrious Ancestor)
"Liè Zǔ,"
(It is) a sacrifice to Zhōng Zōng.
Alas, illustrious ancestor!
(You) have order and thereby blessings.
Greatly bestow unending (favors),
Extending to where you are.
Having prepared clear wine,
Grant me your perfect accomplishment.
Also there is harmonious broth,
Already prepared and made even.
The assembled (spirits) arrive silently,
At this time, there is no strife.
Grant us long life,
And yellow old age without end.
The carriage-ends are neatly fitted, the yokes correctly placed,
The eight bells jingle musically.
We come to present and to offer,
I receive the mandate, a widespread assistance.
From Heaven descends prosperity,
Abundant years, overflowing!
Come to present, come to offer,
Extending blessings without limit.
I look to the seasonal sacrifices,
The impending arrival of the descendant of Tāng!
"Liè Zǔ": one chapter,
Twenty-two lines.
303 "Xuán Niǎo"
"Xuán Niǎo" (Dark Bird),
Is for the sacrifice to Gāo Zōng.
Heaven commissioned the dark bird,
It descended and gave birth to Shāng.
They settled in the vast land of Yīn.
The ancient Emperor commissioned Wǔ Tāng,
To rectify the regions in all four directions.
He then commissioned his successors,
To possess all the nine provinces.
The ancestors of Shāng,
Received the mandate without fail,
Down to the grandsons and sons of Wǔ Dīng.
The grandsons and sons of Wǔ Dīng!
King Wǔ was never defeated.
Dragon banners with ten chariots,
With great offerings they received it.
The borders of the state extended a thousand *lǐ*,
Where the people dwell,
Founding the boundaries of the four seas.
From the four seas they come to make offering,
Coming to make offering, in multitude,
Bright and great is the River.
Yīn received the Mandate, all was fitting,
The hundred blessings, what were they?
"Xuán Niǎo", one chapter,
Twenty-two lines.
304 "Cháng Fā"
"Cháng Fā,"
Is a great sacrifice.
Profoundly wise was Shāng!
Long hair was their auspicious sign.
The flood was vast,
Yǔ laid out the regions of the lower earth.
Beyond, the great states were the borders,
The extent of the land was made long.
Yǒu Sōng was about to depart,
The Di established a son, and Shāng was born!
Xuán Wáng energetically governed!
He received the small states, and made them prosper,
He received the large states, and made them prosper.
Following his footsteps, never overstepping,
Thus his inspections were ever vigorous.
Xiāng Tǔ was majestic,
Beyond the seas, there were boundaries!
Dì mìng bù wéi! The Mandate of the Lord is not to be disobeyed!
Zhì yú Tāng Qí. It reached Tāng Qí.
Tāng jiàng bù chí, Tāng's descent was not slow,
Shèng jìng rì jī. The sage's reverence daily increased.
Zhāo jiǎ chí chí; The bright blessings came slowly;
Shàngdì shì zhī, To God he was reverent,
Dì mìng shì yú jiǔ wéi. The Lord's Mandate extended to the nine regions.
Shòu xiǎo qiú dà qiú, He received the small jade and the large jade,
Wèi xià guó zhuì liú, To adorn the banners of the lower states,
Hé tiān zhī xiū. What Heavenly blessing!
Bù jìng bù qiú, Not striving, not anxious,
Bù gāng bù róu, Not rigid, not yielding,
Fū zhèng yōu yōu: Spreading governance with ease:
Bǎi lù shì qiú! The hundred blessings gathered!
Shòu xiǎo gòng dà gòng, He received the small offerings and the large offerings,
Wèi xià guó jùn páng, To be a mighty support for the lower states,
Hé tiān zhī lóng. What Heavenly favor!
Fū zòu qí yǒng: Displaying his valor:
Bù zhèn bù dòng, Not startling, not agitated,
Bù nǎn bù sǒng. Not fearful, not alarmed.
Bǎi lù shì zǒng! The hundred blessings were gathered!
Wǔ Wáng zài pèi, King Wǔ raised his pennons,
Yǒu qián bǐng yuè. With reverence, he grasped the battle-axe.
Rú huǒ liè liè, Like blazing fire,
Zé mò wǒ gǎn hé. Then none dared to stop us.
Bāo yǒu sān niè, The clump had three shoots,
Mò suì mò dá. None could flourish, none could succeed.
Jiǔ yǒu yǒu jié: The Nine Regions were defined:
Wéi Gù jì fá, Wéi and Gù were already attacked,
Kūn Wú Xià Jié! Kūn Wú and Xià Jié!
Xī zài zhōng yè, Formerly, in the middle age,
Yǒu zhèn qiě yè. There was a great and awesome tremor.
Yǔn yě tiānzǐ! Truly, the Son of Heaven!
Jiàng yǔ qīngshì, [He sent down for me, his ministers,]
shí wéi Ā Héng, [truly he was Ā Héng,]
shí zuǒyòu Shāng Wáng! [truly he assisted the Shāng king!]
"Cháng Fà" qī zhāng, [The "Cháng Fà" has seven stanzas,]
yī zhāng bā jù, [one stanza has eight lines,]
sì zhāng zhāng qī jù, [four stanzas each have seven lines,]
yī zhāng jiǔ jù, [one stanza has nine lines,]
yī zhāng liù jù. [one stanza has six lines.]
305 "Yīn Wǔ"
"Yīn Wǔ", [The "Yīn Wǔ"]
sì Gāo Zōng yě. [is a sacrifice to Gāo Zōng.]
Tà bǐ Yīn wǔ! [How martial was the Yīn army!]
Fèn fá Jīng Chǔ. [Vigorously attacking Jīng and Chǔ.]
Mí rù qí zǔ, [Deeply penetrating their defenses,]
póu Jīng zhī lǚ. [We gathered in the spoils of Jīng.]
Yǒu jié qí suǒ, [We brought order to those regions,]
Tāng sūn zhī xù! [the descendants of Tāng continued!]
Wéi nǚ Jīng Chǔ! [Ah, you of Jīng and Chǔ!]
Jū guó nán xiāng. [Dwelling in the southern regions of the state.]
In the past there was Chéng Tāng:
From those Dī and Qiāng peoples,
None dared not come to offer tribute,
None dared not come to acknowledge his sovereignty,
Saying, "Shāng is the constant!"
Heaven's mandate is broad,
Establishing the capital upon Yǔ's accomplishments:
As the yearly affairs come to be managed,
Do not let misfortune befall me!
The sowing and reaping are not neglected!
Heaven's mandate sends down its inspection,
The people below are held in awe.
Neither presumptuous nor excessive,
Daring not to be idle or remiss.
Mandating the lower states,
Establishing their blessings.
The city of Shāng is grand and imposing,
The center of the four quarters.
Bright is its fame,
Pure is its spiritual power.
May we have longevity, prosperity, and peace,
To protect our descendants!
Ascending that Jǐng Mountain,
The pines and cypresses are rounded.
They are cut and moved,
And then squared reverently.
The pine rafters are long,
The columns are regularly spaced,
The sleeping chambers are completed in great peace!
"Yīn Wǔ" has six stanzas,
Three stanzas have six lines each,
Two stanzas have seven lines each,
